title: 齐次裁剪与透视插值：从投影矩阵到光栅化
description: 投影约定、齐次裁剪、属性透视校正、数值稳健性和可重复验证
turns: 从右手坐标系推导透视投影矩阵，明确相机朝向、近远裁剪面、齐次坐标和 NDC 深度范围。用 LaTeX 展示变换顺序，解释为什么透视除法不能提前到齐次裁剪之前。
推导三角形与齐次裁剪平面的交点参数，说明顶点位于相机后方或 w 接近零时的处理。写出完整的 Sutherland–Hodgman 齐次裁剪伪代码，并分析退化边与浮点容差。
用 Python 实现齐次裁剪和三角扇重建，提供跨越近裁剪面、跨越视锥侧面、完全可见与完全不可见的固定输入，并用断言验证裁剪后顶点满足所有平面约束。
从屏幕重心坐标推导纹理坐标的透视正确插值公式，给出可运行代码对比线性屏幕插值与透视插值，解释深度插值、倒数 w 和属性插值的不同约定。
用 Markdown 表格比较不同投影深度约定、普通与反向深度的数值精度特征，设计验证裁剪接缝、共享边一致性和远近深度精度的测试方案，指出具体实现中应统一的坐标与符号规则。

title: OFDM：循环前缀、频域均衡与误差预算
turns: 用 LaTeX 从离散线性卷积推导 OFDM 循环前缀足够长时的循环卷积模型，说明 DFT 对角化和子载波频域均衡。设置一个虚构的三抽头信道，明确每个变量的单位和索引约定。
推导零迫与 MMSE 单抽头均衡器，比较深衰落处的噪声放大，代入前面的三抽头信道计算几个指定子载波上的系数。所有数字仅作教学例子。
写完整 Python/NumPy 仿真，固定随机种子完成 QPSK、IFFT、循环前缀、信道、噪声和均衡，输出比特错误率及 EVM。禁止省略核心函数，加入无噪声恢复、功率归一化和前缀长度三类断言。
用 Markdown 表格比较前缀不足、载波频偏、采样偏差和信道估计偏差的误差特征，给出可区分这些错误的数值检查，并用 LaTeX 推导一个简化频偏引起的子载波泄漏例子。
写一份较长的工程教学报告，汇总链路预算、前缀开销、导频密度与统计置信区间，解释仿真如何支持或不能支持实际系统结论。提供逐项复现实验步骤和失败诊断清单。

title: 有限域编码：Reed–Solomon 擦除恢复
turns: 用 LaTeX 从有限域多项式求值定义一个教学用 Reed–Solomon 码，明确 GF(17) 上的消息系数、求值点、码长、维数和最小距离。用一组假想消息逐项算出编码结果。
从拉格朗日插值推导擦除恢复，说明可恢复的擦除数量与码维数的关系，手算两个不同的擦除位置集合，并检查恢复出的系数与原消息一致。
写只用 Python 标准库的完整编码与擦除恢复程序，实现模逆、插值和输入校验。给出固定随机种子的随机消息测试、最大可恢复擦除测试及不足观测时必须失败的测试。
用 Markdown 表格比较求值编码、系统编码、复制和 XOR 奇偶校验，列出冗余、擦除能力、运算成本及假设。用前面的参数计算存储开销，解释擦除与未知错误的区别。
写一份较长的工程教学报告，讨论校验和定位擦除、分片元数据、符号序和截断输入的风险，提出可重复的恢复验证流程。保留完整公式与代码引用，避免宣称该简化实现已经适合生产部署。

Write complete runnable standard-library Python for round-robin allocation, EF1 checks and exhaustive Pareto-improvement search for small instances. Fix the random seed and assert behavior for zero values, ties and fewer items than participants.

Use a Markdown table to compare EF, EF1, EFX, proportionality and Pareto optimality across definitions, compatibility, verification cost and guarantees of round-robin. Distinguish proofs from observations on the example.

Write a long algorithm audit with complexity derivations, counterexample tables, pseudocode and property-based test designs. Explain how participant order, tie-breaking, random seeds and nonadditive preferences affect conclusions.

Write a long verification audit with equations, state tables and pseudocode. Explain state explosion, abstraction, environment assumptions and how to replay and minimize a counterexample without claiming exhaustive verification from random tests.

Use a Markdown table to compare BFS per query, union-find for insertions only, rollback union-find offline and fully dynamic online methods across semantics, time costs and implementation constraints.

Write a long algorithm audit with complexity equations, state tables, pseudocode and minimized counterexample traces. Show how to validate rollback snapshots and distinguish testing evidence from a correctness proof.

title: Minimum cost flow: residual networks and dual potentials
turns: Formulate a capacitated minimum cost flow problem using inline and display LaTeX. Define supplies, conservation, capacities and costs, and derive the role of node potentials and reduced costs.
Work through a small numerical residual-network example with reverse arcs. Show an augmenting path, its bottleneck, the updated flow and a check of conservation and objective cost.

Create a Markdown comparison table for cycle canceling, successive shortest paths and network simplex, including assumptions, complexity and negative-cost handling. Include an English-Chinese glossary.

Explain how to verify optimality using reduced costs and complementary slackness. Provide an infeasible example, a reproducible test plan and precise limits of the algorithm when lower bounds or negative cycles are present.

title: Integer algorithms: extended gcd and Diophantine solution lattices
turns: Derive extended Euclidean algorithm invariants and the Bezout identity in LaTeX. Explain how they solve two variable linear Diophantine equations with a worked numerical example.
For 84x+30y=18, derive all integer solutions and count those within specified finite bounds. Compare truncation toward zero versus floor division for negative boundary calculations.

Provide complete standard library Python for sign safe extended gcd, parametric solutions and bounded solution counting. Include zero coefficients, negative coefficients and unsatisfiable cases with executable tests.
Create a Markdown comparison table for extended gcd, enumeration, integer programming and lattice basis methods with input ranges, complexity and correctness assumptions. Add a bilingual glossary.

Design fixed seed differential tests against exhaustive small integer enumeration. Write a detailed report with LaTeX complexity analysis, failure case tables and full reproducible code, distinguishing proof from empirical verification.

title: Weighted rendezvous hashing and shard movement
turns: Derive weighted rendezvous hashing from exponential races in LaTeX. State independence and hashing assumptions, and explain shard assignment probabilities.
Give a worked numerical example of three weighted servers. Show how adding or removing a server changes assignments while preserving unaffected rankings.

Provide complete runnable standard library Python using deterministic cryptographic hashes and explicit uniform conversion. Test weight ratios, zero weights and membership changes with a fixed seed key corpus.
Create a Markdown comparison table for modulo hashing, hash rings, jump hashing and weighted rendezvous by balance, movement, weight support and operational cost. Add a bilingual glossary.

Write a detailed experimental report measuring load deviation and reassignment fractions for heterogeneous weights. Include formulas, reproducible code and result tables. Discuss correlated keys, finite samples and implementation stability.

title: Database isolation: write skew, serialization graphs and MVCC snapshots
turns: Explain snapshot isolation using a fictional seat-reservation database. Define versions, transaction read and write sets, and a consistency invariant with LaTeX; include a concrete two-transaction example.
Construct a write-skew schedule, derive its serialization graph and distinguish conflict serializability from snapshot consistency. Show the schedule as a Markdown table.
Write complete runnable Python implementing a tiny deterministic MVCC simulator with begin, read, write and commit. Include tests for lost updates, write skew and non-conflicting transactions.

Compare snapshot isolation, strict two-phase locking and serializable snapshot isolation in a Markdown table. Explain blocking, aborted work and anomaly detection with an English and Chinese glossary.

Design an exhaustive schedule enumeration for three transactions and four keys. Give detailed pseudo-code, graph-cycle equations, runnable tests and a reproducible results table; justify every anomaly classification.

title: Spherical cartography: cube-map face coordinates and seam continuity
turns: Generate an actual image using Imagen: an original annotated educational illustration of a globe surrounded by its six cube-map faces, indicating shared edges and axes. Then define the coordinate frames and explain the mapping assumptions in prose.
Derive forward direction-to-face and inverse face-to-direction maps in LaTeX. State the exact tie-breaking rule on edges and corners, and prove reconstruction up to normalization.
Provide complete runnable Python with only the standard library to map vectors to cube faces and back, with randomized round-trip tests and explicit edge/corner cases.
Compare cube-map, equirectangular and octahedral parameterizations in a Markdown table covering area distortion, seam rules, storage and interpolation. Add an English and Chinese glossary.

Write a detailed numerical audit of seam continuity and finite precision. Include error norms, test vectors, threshold tables and reproducible code without suggesting rendering agreement proves geometric correctness.

title: Integer modules: Smith normal form, invariant factors and Diophantine feasibility
turns: Explain Smith normal form for a small integer matrix and define unimodular row/column transformations, invariant factors and divisibility conditions using LaTeX.

Derive a constructive elementary-operation algorithm for two-by-two and three-by-three integer matrices. Track transformation matrices explicitly and discuss why naive remainder reduction can break divisibility.
Provide complete runnable Python implementing exact-integer reduction with independently verified U*A*V=D tests, unimodular determinant checks and randomly generated small cases.
Compare Smith and Hermite normal forms in a Markdown table covering uniqueness conventions, preserved modules and computational costs. Give an English and Chinese glossary.

Design a reproducible Diophantine-system feasibility audit using invariant factors. Include exact examples, counterexamples, solution parameterizations, rank-deficient cases and a thorough validation table.

title: Binary alloys: phase diagrams and lever-rule reasoning
description: Synthetic phase-diagram illustration, mass balance, reproducible phase fractions, tables and solidification report.
turns: Generate an original educational illustration of a fictional binary eutectic alloy phase diagram with clearly separated liquid, alpha, beta and two-phase regions. Explain the schematic axes and labels in English and Chinese, and explicitly identify all numerical values as hypothetical.
Use LaTeX to derive the lever rule from total mass and solute conservation. Work through one hypothetical tie-line example, state the concentration basis and verify both phase fractions sum to one.

Write complete runnable Python using only the standard library to compute phase fractions for hypothetical tie lines. Validate physical bounds and reject inconsistent endpoints; include deterministic assertions and a bisection routine for a fictional temperature-dependent boundary.

Create a Markdown table comparing equilibrium cooling, finite-rate solidification and diffusion-limited segregation. Separate model assumptions from measured facts and include bilingual terminology and dimensional checks.

Write a detailed methods report about numerical conditioning near a phase boundary, uncertainty propagation and why a schematic diagram cannot predict a real alloy. Include algorithm pseudocode, reproducible synthetic parameter tables and LaTeX error estimates.

turns: Define dominators and immediate dominators on a synthetic control-flow graph using LaTeX set equations. Include a branch merge and loop, explicitly identify reachable nodes, and distinguish dominance from postdominance.

Derive an iterative fixed-point dominator algorithm and dominance-frontier construction. Hand-calculate a small graph with a back edge, state the initialization and termination invariant, and explain treatment of unreachable blocks.

Write complete runnable Python standard-library code for dominators, dominance frontiers and iterated phi placement. Include deterministic graph examples, assertions for entry and unreachable nodes, and a variable defined on two branches.

Use a Markdown table to compare naive fixed-point dominance, tree-based dominance and pruned versus unpruned SSA. Describe time and space bounds with clear assumptions, and include English and Chinese terminology.

Write a detailed compiler methods report about renaming stacks, loop phi nodes and preserving semantics during SSA destruction. Include counterexample graphs, pseudocode, reproducible tests and a LaTeX invariant, separating proved properties from implementation heuristics.

title: Polarization optics: Brewster angle and Jones matrices
description: Original polarization illustration, dielectric-interface equations, runnable matrix calculations, comparison tables and an uncertainty report.
turns: Generate an original educational image showing a hypothetical laser beam incident on a dielectric interface near the Brewster angle, with incident, reflected and transmitted rays and clearly distinguished s and p polarization directions. Explain the schematic in English and Chinese; label all numerical parameters as synthetic.

Use LaTeX to derive the Brewster-angle condition and define the Jones vectors and coordinate conventions for a lossless isotropic interface. Work one hypothetical refractive-index example and check the angular and unit conventions.

Write complete runnable Python with NumPy to compute normalized Jones-vector transformations and a synthetic intensity sweep. Include deterministic assertions for limiting angles, polarization normalization and valid refractive indices, and explicitly distinguish amplitude from power coefficients.

Create a Markdown table comparing Jones and Mueller descriptions, assumptions about coherence and polarization, input dimensions and failure cases. Add bilingual terminology and clearly label any illustrative numerical results.

Write a detailed laboratory-methods report using only hypothetical data. Analyze angular calibration, near-zero reflected p intensity and numerical sensitivity; provide pseudocode, LaTeX uncertainty estimates and a reproducible parameter table, and explain which effects the idealized model excludes.

title: Discrete control systems: observability and state reconstruction
description: Linear-system observability, Gramian derivations, executable reconstruction code, comparative tables and numerical-conditioning analysis.
turns: Define finite-horizon observability for a synthetic discrete-time linear system using LaTeX. Construct a small two-state example and derive its stacked output equations, distinguishing observability from controllability and stability.

Derive the finite-horizon observability Gramian and prove the rank criterion for exact state reconstruction in the noiseless model. Hand-calculate an observable and an unobservable example, stating the horizon and assumptions explicitly.

Write complete runnable Python with NumPy for simulation and least-squares initial-state reconstruction. Use fixed random seeds for synthetic observation noise, check dimensions and matrix rank, and include deterministic exact-recovery and deliberately unobservable test cases.

Use a Markdown table to compare direct inversion, QR and singular-value decomposition for reconstruction. Include time and memory bounds with assumptions, threshold selection, English/Chinese terminology and an example sensitivity comparison.

Write a detailed technical report about near-unobservability, sensor placement and horizon length. Include reproducible synthetic parameter tables, algorithm pseudocode, a LaTeX error bound and explicit distinctions between structural observability, numerical conditioning and unsupported performance claims.

Write a long mathematical validation report on conservation, nonnegative state constraints, numerical rank tolerances and the difference between stoichiometric feasibility and kinetic behavior. Include reproducible pseudocode, counterexamples and a bilingual glossary.
